description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/malformed-checkov.json -- a document written under a KNOWN artifact name whose content is not that writer's native shape. It states a HALT, not rows, despite the .rows.json suffix this folder's naming convention requires: the suffix names the folder's contract (one expected file per fixture), not the shape of every outcome. Every value below was derived by reading the fixture and the authored tables in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py, and each is asserted programmatically by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_shape_routing_negative.py rather than taken on trust.
tool_note: The tool IS resolved here, which is what distinguishes this fixture from expected/unknown-shape.rows.json: the name routing keys on is one of the nine, so the writer is known and only its document shape is wrong. That is the whole of this case -- a known filename is not a licence to adapt whatever it contains.
null_field_note: scanner_class and adapter are null rather than omitted, so a generic loader reads this file with the same keys as the positive expected files in this folder. They are null because the halt precedes adapter selection and row construction: no row exists to carry a scanner_class (the class the checkov writer's rows would have carried is misconfig, from shape.SCANNER_CLASS_BY_TOOL, and it is deliberately not recorded as this document's outcome), and no adapter module is named, imported or called.

fixture.authored_note: An authored document, not captured tool output. It is the shape of a real Checkov object-form report -- check_type, results, summary -- with the one member the signature requires broken: results carries a STRING where a JSON object is required. Everything else is deliberately plausible, because a fixture that looked obviously wrong would not exercise the case: what makes this dangerous is that every interior validator accepts it. Nothing in it is a finding, a secret, a credential or a token, no value is a measurement of anything, and it names no filesystem path.
fixture.why_it_is_not_named_checkov_json: This folder already holds fixtures/checkov.json, the captured positive fixture, so a second file cannot take that name. The negative test therefore routes this document under the artifact filename its writer uses (see routed_as below) rather than under the fixture's own filename, which resolves to no tool at all.

routed_as.subject: checkov.json
routed_as.second_subject_note: Both forms are asserted, because a run resolves the path form (shape.route_artifact over an entry in harness/artifacts/raw/) while a bare filename is what the authored tables hold. Only the filename component is read; neither path is opened, and no absolute path appears in this file or in the test.
routed_as.fixture_name_resolution_note: shape.resolve_tool("malformed-checkov.json") is None. Asserted by the test so the halt below cannot be passing for the wrong reason: routed under its own name this document would halt with shape.REASON_UNRECOGNIZED_ARTIFACT_NAME, which is a different condition owned by expected/unknown-shape.rows.json.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.conjunction_authority: AAP 0.5.4: an artifact is SARIF when it carries version "2.1.0" together with a runs array -- those two together are the test.
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: The document is a mapping, so the first condition holds. It carries no version key, so doc.get("version") is None and None == "2.1.0" is False. It carries no runs key, so isinstance(None, list) is False. BOTH halves fail, which is why the native signature below is the test that decides this document's fate.

native_signature.authority: normalize.shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["checkov"], derived from AAP 0.5.4's per-shape record-location table
native_signature.expected: either a JSON object carrying "results" whose value is a JSON object, or a JSON array whose every element is a JSON object carrying a "results" object (the multi-framework form). An empty or absent "failed_checks" inside "results" is legitimate: this dataset emits failed checks only, and a framework that failed nothing still reports
native_signature.expected_note: Recorded verbatim and asserted equal to the signature's own statement string, so this file cannot describe a requirement the implementation does not make.
native_signature.why_it_fails: The top level is an object, which this signature accepts, and it carries the required results key -- so a presence-only test would pass it. The value is a JSON string, where a JSON object is required, so the container the adapter walks and the container reconcile._count_checkov counts does not exist at all.
native_signature.what_is_deliberately_not_required: Nothing inside results is read: an empty failed_checks, or a results object carrying no failed_checks member at all, is a legitimate report and satisfies this signature. The signature tests the container's presence and type, never its length, so a framework that failed nothing is never mistaken for a malformed artifact.

counting_traversal.note: This is the measured reason the halt has to exist. The counting traversal reads results through its own _as_mapping and contributes zero for a string, and the adapter's own container handling contributes zero rows and zero rejections -- so before this fix the identity balanced at 0 = 0 + 0 over a malformed document, parse status read clean, and nothing downstream could tell that apart from a scan that found nothing. AAP 0.5.4 requires a halt rather than a best-effort parse, and AAP 0.9.2 lists the condition among those that stop the run.
counting_traversal.traversal_unchanged: reconcile.py's traversal is deliberately not hardened into a second shape test: its value is that it shares no code and no judgement with the row builder. The halt belongs one layer up, in shape.py.

named_halt_requirement.statement: A KeyError or TypeError escaping a half-attempted parse is a FAILURE, not a pass: it carries no reason, names no artifact, quotes no expected signature and cannot be told apart from a defect in the normalizer itself. The test asserts the exact type with assertIs(type(error), shape.UnknownArtifactShape), never Exception.
named_halt_requirement.raised_by_the_shape_layer: The exception must come from normalize.shape.route or normalize.shape.route_artifact -- the module that owns the decision -- rather than from an adapter reached with a document whose shape was never established.

halt.reason_inventory: shape.HALT_REASONS, the closed set of four: unrecognized-artifact-name, unsupported-document-type, sarif-producer-artifact-not-sarif, native-shape-unrecognized.
halt.reason_note: Not the name reason: the name resolves to checkov. Not the container reason: an object top level is a supported container. The halt is attributable to the document not being this writer's native shape, and the test asserts all three facts so a report cannot send a reader after the wrong defect.
halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind

observed_attributes.stem_note: For this reason the stem carries the canonical tool identifier rather than a filename: the writer is known by the time the signature is tested.

message_must_carry: the observed structure where that signature required a container
halt.details_method: shape.UnknownArtifactShape.details() returns the same facts as a flat JSON-serialisable mapping, adding expected_artifacts, signature_tool, expected_signature and signature_observation. The test asserts json.dumps over it succeeds, because harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.json has to carry the halt record.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: a rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns its artifact, and this document never reaches an adapter. The test asserts the non-membership of the reason and the exception name over paths.REJECT_CLASSES programmatically.

halt.reason_literal_divergence: This value was authored as the literal 'native-signature-mismatch' against a tree where the signature check owned a reason of its own. In the delivered tree that constant and shape.REASON_NATIVE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED are ONE literal -- 'native-shape-unrecognized' -- because a known artifact name whose document does not carry that writer's structure is one condition however it is detected, and two literals for it would put a reason outside shape.HALT_REASONS, which the router's own inventory is asserted closed over. reason_constant is unchanged and is what the test compares against; the literal recorded here is the value that constant holds in this tree.

parse.why_well_formedness_is_the_point: A document that fails to parse is stopped by the parser and no shape decision is reached. It is precisely a document that parses perfectly, carries a known artifact name and reads plausibly that tempts a best-effort parse -- and that is the case this fixture puts in front of the implementation.

counts.raw_count_unit_note: Null rather than 0: a count unit is a property of a document of the right shape, and this document has none. What the traversal would return over it anyway is recorded above under counting_traversal.would_return, where it is evidence about the defect rather than a reconciliation figure.
counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes any record traversal, so no count unit exists to reconcile against

rows_note: Explicitly empty, and empty for a different reason than a clean scan is empty: the pipeline stopped, it did not look and find nothing. Zero rows reported alongside a successful parse status is exactly the outcome this fixture exists to make impossible.
guarded_failure: A permissive shape layer does not raise on this document -- it hands it to the checkov adapter, which reads no failed_checks, emits zero rows and zero rejections, and reports success. The independent counting traversal returns zero as well, so the reconciliation identity balances and parse status reads clean. Every downstream signal is identical to a Checkov run that found nothing, and no signal anywhere says the artifact was unreadable.

assertions: shape.route over this fixture's parsed document under the subject checkov.json raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape, and the raised type is exactly that class.
shape.route_artifact over harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json and the same document raises the same reason, so both entry points halt.
error.reason equals shape.REASON_NATIVE_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH, and is neither of the other two members of shape.HALT_REASONS.
error.signature_tool is checkov and error.expected_signature equals shape.NATIVE_SIGNATURES["checkov"].statement, which this file records verbatim.
error.signature_observation records the required key, the required type and the observed type, and those match the values recorded here.
shape.is_sarif over the document is False and shape.matches_native_signature("checkov", doc) is False.
reconcile.count_records("checkov", doc) is 0 -- the false-clean this halt prevents, asserted rather than asserted about.
No adapter module is imported by the halting routing call.
The rows array is empty, the rejection total is 0, and neither the reason nor the exception name is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES.
shape.resolve_tool over the fixture's own filename is None, so the subject the test routes under is the artifact filename and not the fixture name.
The fixture's sha256, byte size, top-level type and top-level keys equal the values recorded here, so this file cannot drift from the document it describes.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: AAP 0.5.4 mandates a negative test asserting that a native artifact does not route to the SARIF adapter; that assertion is owned by the same test file over the captured native fixtures. This fixture extends it in the direction the review found open: a KNOWN filename whose content is not that writer's native shape must halt rather than become a clean zero-result.

related_fixtures.the_captured_positive: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov.json -- the object form this document imitates, whose results IS an object and which routes normally.
related_fixtures.the_other_legitimate_shape: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json -- the multi-framework array form, which satisfies the array half of the same signature.
related_fixtures.the_fall_through: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/unknown-shape.json -- a document under an UNRECOGNISED name, which halts for a different reason and whose expected file states it.
related_fixtures.the_uncovered_array_case: A checkov array form whose element is not an object, or whose element's results is a string, fails the same signature and is exercised directly in oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_checkov_adapter.py rather than by a sixth fixture here.
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's, and each expected file states its own.

prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or redacted-secret placeholder appears in any field of this file or its fixture (this tree is committed to git). No finding is judged -- nothing here is called real, important, a false positive or a duplicate. Nothing is deduplicated. No tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape decision and the halt it must produce, and nothing else.
